Read in full: daemon/src/nemesis_core_daemon.adb, daemon/src/nemesis-core-authority_store.ads/.adb, daemon/tests/nemesis_authority_store_tests.adb, kernel/src/nemesis-kernel-capabilities.ads/.adb, kernel/src/nemesis-kernel-approvals.ads/.adb, kernel/src/nemesis-kernel-types.ads, daemon/src/nemesis-core-json.ads/.adb, plus commit/durability paths of nemesis-core-mission_store.ads/.adb and nemesis-core-ledger.adb, and the baseline->subject git diff of the daemon main. gaps.evidence: daemon/src/nemesis-core-authority_store.adb:37-48 (errors ignored), :146-150 (Success independent of dir sync); contrast with the file-level F_FULLFSYNC which is treated as fatal at :136-140. Invariant text in nemesis-core-authority_store.ads:47-51 promises durable replacement before the authorization event.
gaps.impact: Full_Sync_Directory (:37-48) ignores both open failure and fcntl failure, and Write_Record sets Success := Renamed regardless of directory-sync outcome (:146-150). Persist_Consumed_Approval can therefore report Authority_OK while the rename of the consumed record is not yet durable. In the worst-case crash window the on-disk approval could revert to Active while the subsequent Action_Authorized ledger event (whose own file F_FULLFSYNC is error-checked, ledger.adb:339-342) survived — narrowing the stated 'consumed-before-commit, never replayable' guarantee from always to almost-always. The identical best-effort pattern exists in mission_store.adb:36-45 and ledger.adb:35-44.
gaps.precondition: Power loss shortly after authorize_action, combined with a failed directory F_FULLFSYNC (e.g., fd exhaustion causing C_Open to fail, or fcntl error) and filesystem metadata-journal ordering that lets the later ledger append become durable while the earlier consumed-approval rename is lost.
gaps.remediation: Make Full_Sync_Directory return a Boolean (or status) and have Write_Record treat directory open/fcntl failure exactly like the file F_FULLFSYNC failure — Success := False — so Persist_Consumed_Approval refuses and authorize_action fails closed before Commit_Event. Apply the same propagation in mission_store and ledger for symmetry.

gaps.evidence: daemon/src/nemesis_core_daemon.adb:38-42 (comment), :277-278 (Parent_Grant_Byte_Budget), :390 (Maximum_Bytes => Parent.Maximum_Bytes per child); kernel Authorize checks only per-action Estimated_Bytes <= Grant.Maximum_Bytes (capabilities.adb:18-19). protocols/local-core-v1.md:22-23 documents only a per-action byte-budget binding, so the protocol contract itself is not violated.
gaps.impact: The comment at daemon.adb:38-40 calls the parent grant 'the mission's whole reviewed write budget', but Maximum_Bytes is never decremented across actions: every derived child receives the full Parent.Maximum_Bytes (4,096) at :390, so N approved actions may each estimate up to 4,096 bytes. Because each action still requires its own human-created one-shot approval bound to an exact action digest, per-action authority remains human-gated and no lane invariant requires cumulative accounting — but the comment overstates the enforced property and could mislead future maintainers into relying on a mission-wide cap.
gaps.remediation: Either reword the comment to 'per-action reviewed write budget', or implement cumulative decrement (persist remaining budget in the parent grant record on each authorization) if mission-wide budgeting is the intended contract.

findings.summary: Full_Sync_Directory in the authority store ignores open() and fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC) failures, and Write_Record reports success based solely on rename. The consumed-approval record can be reported durable while its rename is not yet synced to the directory, slightly weakening the documented consumed-before-commit replay guarantee under a coincident sync failure and power loss.
findings.title: Directory F_FULLFSYNC failures silently ignored in authority-store durability chain

findings.summary: The parent grant's Maximum_Bytes (4,096) is not decremented across actions; each approved action's child grant receives the full budget. Enforcement matches the protocol doc (per-action binding) but not the daemon comment's mission-wide framing. Per-action authority remains human-gated by one-shot approvals, so this is documentation-level only.
findings.title: 'Whole reviewed write budget' comment overstates non-cumulative per-action byte budget
